data.description:
## What is wrong

The compaction sweep's stand-aside check cannot see a writer that is waiting for the store write lock, so a long sweep starves canonical writes until they time out.

`_sweep_should_yield` (`src/rebar/_commands/compact.py`) calls `write_lock_is_busy` between tickets. At that moment the sweep has just released the lock, so the probe reports "not busy" unless the waiting writer happened to win the race in that instant. The sweep then takes the lock for the next ticket. A writer polling with its 181 s budget (30 s x 2 attempts x 3 passes) keeps losing.

## Evidence

Production MCP host, 2026-11-01 21:00-21:35 PST (journald `rebar-mcp`, read-only SSM):

- One sweep (`op=compact-sweep`, pid 1427) committed 10 `COMPACT` events between 21:03:13 and 21:34:49, holding the lock 100-165 s per ticket.
- A waiting writer's retry log shows the holder's `held=` fall from 161 s to 25 s within one wait: the sweep released and re-took the lock while the writer was still waiting.
- 3 writes failed with `flock: could not acquire lock after 181s ... op=compact-sweep`: a plan-review attestation at 21:08:30, and 2 `REVIEW_RESULT` sidecars at 21:10:36 and 21:11:32. That lost a billed PASS (`b505-d66e-86b3-4446`) and a billed BLOCK's findings (`2041-75d6-2a2f-4be9`).
- The build that ran included `f3cb9223d8c` (bug `graspable-fabled-skylark`, history walks moved out of the lock), so this is a different path to the same outage.

Local reproduction (current main, real `rebar._store.lock`, separate processes): a holder loop that holds for 1 s, releases, calls `write_lock_is_busy`, and re-takes the lock. A writer in another process waits with a 3 s budget. Result: writer `LockTimeout` after 3.03 s; all 6 yield probes returned `False`.

## Second effect: real divergence for the length of the sweep

The sweep commits each fold locally and pushes once at the end ("Pushes remain batched"). On the host clone, `HEAD` gained 10 unpushed `COMPACT` commits while fetches fast-forwarded `origin/tickets` 4 times. From 21:06:15 to the 21:35:01 merge the clone had genuinely diverged, so every gate's freshness check correctly refused with `stale-store` for about 29 minutes.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A writer waiting for the store lock while a sweep runs gets the lock before its budget expires. Checked by: a test with a sweep-like holder in one process and a waiting writer in another, asserting the writer acquires the lock.
- [ ] The sweep's unpublished folds do not leave the clone diverged from the shared store for longer than one fold. Checked by: a test asserting the clone has no unpushed sweep commits after each fold when a push target is reachable.
- [ ] `make verify` passes.
data.title: Compaction sweep cannot see a waiting writer, so it starves store writes until they time out
